08-01.s: Chemist Tadeus Reichstein, who shared the 1950 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for isolating adrenal cortex hormones including cortisone and discovering its use in rheumatoid arthritis, died.

08-02.s: German chemist Leopold Gmelin was born; he developed Gmelin's test, a chemical assay used to detect bile pigments in urine samples.
Austrian-born physician Peter Safar, widely remembered as a pioneer of modern cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) and critical care medicine, passed away.

08-03.s: Japanese engineer Koichi Tanaka was born; he shared the 2002 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for developing soft laser desorption mass spectrometry to analyze biological macromolecules such as proteins.
The Texas Heart Institute was founded by surgeon Denton Cooley to research and treat cardiovascular disease, later achieving the first U.S. heart transplant and first artificial heart implant.

08-04.s: American pediatrician and virologist Frederick Chapman Robbins, who shared the 1954 Nobel Prize for cultivating poliovirus in tissue culture, died in Cleveland, Ohio.

08-05.s: Brazilian physician, bacteriologist, and epidemiologist Oswaldo Cruz was born; he founded the Oswaldo Cruz Institute, a leading public health research institution.
Austrian dermatologist Ferdinand Ritter von Hebra, recognized for identifying the parasitic cause of scabies and advancing modern dermatology, passed away.

08-06.s: Scottish bacteriologist and trained surgeon Alexander Fleming was born; his discoveries of lysozyme and penicillin ushered in the antibiotic era and earned him the 1945 Nobel Prize.
German biochemist Feodor Lynen, co-recipient of the 1964 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for his research on cholesterol and fatty acid metabolism, died in Munich.

08-07.s: American immunologist James P. Allison was born; he pioneered immune checkpoint blockade cancer therapy and shared the 2018 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine.
American biochemist Kary Mullis, who won the 1993 Nobel Prize for inventing the polymerase chain reaction (PCR) used across medical diagnostics, died in Newport Beach, California.

08-08.s: American surgeon Robert Holbrook Smith, who co-founded Alcoholics Anonymous, was born in St. Johnsbury, Vermont.
Eye surgeon Svyatoslav Fyodorov was born; in 1974 he developed radial keratotomy (RK), the first surgical procedure to correct myopia.

08-09.s: Under royal license, physician Charles Maitland performed an observed variolation trial on six prisoners at Newgate Prison in London, all of whom survived and demonstrated immunity to smallpox.

08-10.s: German-born Swiss entrepreneur Henri Nestlé, credited with developing early infant formula, was born.
Swedish biochemist Arne Tiselius was born; he won the 1948 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for his research on electrophoresis of serum proteins.

08-11.s: Virologist Max Theiler, who won the 1951 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for developing the 17D yellow fever vaccine, passed away.

08-12.s: American surgeon and World War I military physician Joseph Augustus Blake, noted for advancing the surgical treatment of severe fractures and war wounds, died in Connecticut.
British electrical engineer Sir Godfrey N. Hounsfield, who invented computed tomography (CT) scanning and shared the 1979 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine, passed away.

08-13.s: Hungarian physician Ignaz Semmelweis, pioneer of antiseptic handwashing who dramatically lowered maternity ward mortality from puerperal fever, died in Vienna.
Italian-born American microbiologist Salvador Luria was born; he shared the 1969 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for discoveries on viral replication and genetic structure.

08-14.s: American physician William Henry Beierwaltes, a pioneer in nuclear medicine who advanced radioactive iodine-131 therapy for thyroid cancer and co-developed iobenguane imaging, died.

08-14.t: WHO Declares Mpox Resurgence a Global Public Health Emergency
08-14.s: The WHO Director-General declared the resurgence of mpox in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and neighboring African nations a Public Health Emergency of International Concern.

08-15.s: Biochemist Gerty Cori was born in Prague; in 1947 she became the first woman to win the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for discovering the catalytic conversion of glycogen and the Cori cycle.
American pediatric immunologist Arthur J. Ammann, who discovered in utero HIV transmission and helped develop the first successful pneumococcal vaccine in 1977, passed away.

08-16.s: Microbiologist Selman A. Waksman, who won the 1952 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for soil microbe studies leading to the discovery of streptomycin for tuberculosis, passed away.

08-17.s: American gynecologist John Albertson Sampson was born; he conducted foundational research on endometriosis and has the Sampson artery named in his honor.
The first meeting of the Narcotics Anonymous program for individuals recovering from substance addiction took place in Southern California.

08-18.s: French virologist Luc Montagnier was born in Chabris; he shared the 2008 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine with Françoise Barré-Sinoussi for discovering HIV.

08-19.s: Dutch psychiatrist Anna Terruwe was born; she described emotional deprivation disorder and developed affirmation therapy approaches for obsessive-compulsive disorder.
British microbiologist and geneticist David Hopwood was born; his research elucidated the genetics of antibiotic-producing Streptomyces bacteria.

08-20.t: Ronald Ross Discovers Mosquito Transmission of Malaria
08-20.s: British physician Sir Ronald Ross discovered malaria parasites in female Anopheles mosquitoes, proving how malaria is transmitted to humans, an achievement now commemorated as World Mosquito Day.

08-21.s: American physician Gladys Rowena Henry Dick, who co-developed an antitoxin and vaccine for scarlet fever with her husband George F. Dick, died in Palo Alto, California.

08-22.s: Swiss physician and nutritionist Maximilian Bircher-Benner was born; he championed therapeutic nutrition in clinical care.
Canadian-American scientist James Hillier was born; he co-invented the first successful high-resolution electron microscope in North America, transforming cellular pathology.

08-23.s: American biochemist Thomas A. Steitz was born; he won the 2009 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for elucidating ribosome structure and how antibiotics inhibit ribosomal function.
American virologist Thomas Huckle Weller, who shared the 1954 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for cultivating polioviruses in non-neural human tissue culture, died in Massachusetts.

08-24.s: Biochemist Haim Ernst Wertheimer, recognized as a foundational researcher in lipid and fat metabolism, was born.

Belgian physician and cell biologist Albert Claude was born; he shared the 1974 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for discoveries concerning the structural and functional organization of the cell.

08-25.s: Swiss surgeon Emil Theodor Kocher was born in Bern; he won the 1909 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for his work on the physiology, pathology, and surgery of the thyroid gland.
American virologist Charles M. Rice was born; he shared the 2020 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for the discovery of the hepatitis C virus.

08-26.s: Dutch scientist Antonie van Leeuwenhoek, known as the Father of Microbiology for his pioneering microscopic observations of bacteria, muscle fibers, and blood flow, passed away.
Polish-American medical researcher Albert Sabin was born; he developed the oral polio vaccine that proved instrumental in nearly eradicating poliomyelitis worldwide.

08-27.s: Swiss-American biochemist Edmond H. Fischer, who shared the 1992 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for discovering reversible protein phosphorylation as a biological regulatory switch, died in Seattle.

08-28.s: American physician and pathologist George Hoyt Whipple was born; he shared the 1934 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for discovering liver therapy for pernicious anemia.

08-29.s: German physician Werner Forssmann was born in Berlin; he shared the 1956 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for pioneering cardiac catheterization.
American surgical technician and cardiac surgery pioneer Vivien Thomas, who co-developed the Blalock-Taussig-Thomas shunt for blue baby syndrome, was born in Louisiana.

08-30.s: Swedish chemist Theodor Svedberg was born; he developed analytical ultracentrifugation, enabling scientists to separate and characterize proteins.
American microbiologist Maurice Hilleman was born; he developed more than 40 vaccines, including those for measles, mumps, rubella, hepatitis A and B, chickenpox, and pneumococcal pneumonia.

08-31.s: German physician and physicist Hermann von Helmholtz was born; he measured nerve impulse conduction speed and made foundational contributions to physiological optics and ophthalmology.
Canadian physician and academic Moran Campbell was born; he invented the Venturi mask for controlled oxygen therapy and served as founding chair of McMaster University's Faculty of Health Sciences.
